newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria gets new 10,000-lv note as inflation soars. [CORRECTED 12:49 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria gets new 10,000-lv note as inflation soars. [CORRECTED 12:49 GMT]

text.p: Bulgaria, whose currency is falling rapidly against the dollar, will put into circulation next week (Corrects from "...next year") a 10,000-lev note, the largest denomination so far, the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Thursday.

"The BNB will put into circulation a new note with a par value of 10,000 levs on December 9 to ease large payments amid high inflation," Rozalina Natseva, head of the issue department, told a news conference.
The largest denomination now is a 5,000-lev note, introduced on June 17.
The new note, printed in Germany, depicts Bulgarian artist Vladimir Dimitrov and his work.
The lev has declined from 71 per dollar on January 2 to 415 on December 4 on the interbank forex market.
Official figures show monthly inflation for October was 16.7 percent and cumulative inflation for the first 10 months of 1996 was 195 percent.

Since then the lev has fallen further against the dollar and energy prices have risen further. Fuel prices rose six-fold between January and November and energy prices increased more than 300 percent within the same period.
Natseva declined to say whether the BNB planned to put into circulation larger denomination notes.
"We think it will take a long time before inflation devalues the new note," Natseva said.
Annual inflation for 1996 was expected to top 200 percent, overshooting a government target of some 100 percent.
